introSection.heading: Navigating Princess Cruises' Package Options
introSection.p1: Princess Cruises offers two optional packages designed to make your onboard experience more convenient: Princess Plus and Princess Premier. Both bundle popular services such as drinks, Wi-Fi, crew appreciation, dining, and delivery benefits, but Premier includes a broader selection of extras.
introSection.p2: The right choice depends on how you like to cruise. If you mainly want drinks, internet access, and a few casual dining experiences, Princess Plus may be enough. If you plan to enjoy specialty restaurants, use shore excursion credits, and take advantage of premium benefits, Princess Premier may offer better value.
introSection.p3: This guide compares Princess Plus vs. Princess Premier, including current package prices, dining allowances, beverage limits, Wi-Fi, excursion credits, and the situations in which each option makes sense.

packageBreakdowns.title: What Does Each Princess Package Include?
packageBreakdowns.subtitle: A detailed look at the core inclusions, beverage parameters, and onboard allowances

plus.title: What Does Princess Plus Include?
plus.cost: $70 per person, per day ($75 on Sun & Star Princess)
plus.description: Princess Plus is designed for guests who want several popular onboard services bundled together without paying for the more extensive Premier package.
bullets: Plus Beverage Package: up to 15 eligible alcoholic drinks per day up to $15 each (cocktails, wine by the glass, beer, spirits, fountain sodas, mocktails, specialty coffees, teas, and up to 12 bottles of water daily)
MedallionNet Max Wi-Fi: satellite internet connection for 1 device per guest
Four Casual Dining Meals: 4 qualifying meals per guest per voyage at venues like Alfredo's Pizzeria, Kai Sushi, or Ocean Terrace
Crew Appreciation: daily gratuities covered on behalf of eligible guests under package terms
OceanNow Delivery & Room Service: $14.99 per voyage OceanNow device delivery fee waived and complimentary room-service delivery

premier.title: What Does Princess Premier Include?
premier.cost: $105 per person, per day ($110 on Sun & Star Princess)
premier.description: Princess Premier includes all the core benefits of Princess Plus while adding a substantially broader selection of dining, beverage, connectivity, and premium vacation experiences.
bullets: Premier Beverage Package: unlimited eligible beverages up to $20 each with no daily limit on alcoholic drinks (top-shelf spirits, premium wines, craft cocktails, specialty coffees, mocktails, and bottled water)
Unlimited Specialty & Casual Dining: unlimited qualifying meals at Crown Grill, Sabatini's Italian Trattoria, The Catch by Rudi, and all casual venues
MedallionNet Max Wi-Fi: multi-device connectivity for up to 4 devices per guest simultaneously
Shore Excursion Credit: $100 per guest (6–9 days), $200 (10–20 days), or $300 (21+ days)
Professional Photo Package: unlimited digital photos taken by ship photographers plus 3 printed photos
Reserved Theater Seating: dedicated VIP seating section for production shows in the Princess Theater
OceanNow & Room Service: waived activation fees and complimentary stateroom delivery

categories.title: Which Is Better for Drinks?
categories.description: Princess Plus includes 15 alcoholic drinks per day up to $15 each. Princess Premier includes unlimited eligible drinks up to $20 each with no daily count limit. Both include unlimited specialty coffees, teas, fountain sodas, and 12 bottled waters daily.
categories.bestFor: Choose Plus for moderate drinking under $15/cocktail; choose Premier if you prefer top-shelf spirits, fine wines above $15, or average more than 15 drinks in a day.

categories.title: Which Is Better for Dining?
categories.description: Princess Plus provides 4 casual dining meals per guest for the entire voyage (venues such as Alfredo's or Ocean Terrace) and no specialty dining allowance. Princess Premier provides unlimited qualifying casual and specialty dining meals (Crown Grill, Sabatini's, The Catch).
categories.bestFor: Choose Plus if you love the main dining room and buffet with occasional casual lunches; choose Premier if you want to dine at high-end specialty steakhouses and seafood venues throughout your cruise.

categories.title: Which Is Better for Wi-Fi?
categories.description: Princess Plus covers 1 device per guest on MedallionNet Max. Princess Premier covers up to 4 devices per guest, allowing simultaneous connectivity for smartphones, tablets, smartwatches, and laptops without constant logging out and in.
categories.bestFor: Choose Plus if you only connect one phone to stay in touch; choose Premier for digital nomads, multi-device families, or remote business needs.

purchaseSteps.title: Can You Purchase Princess Plus or Premier After Booking?
purchaseSteps.subtitle: Important rules, deadlines, and upgrading instructions before your voyage

steps.title: Book Pre-Cruise (96-Hour Deadline)
steps.description: Always purchase your package more than four days (96 hours) before departure via Princess Manage Booking or your travel advisor to secure the published pre-cruise rate. Purchasing onboard or within four days incurs an extra $5 per person, per day surcharge.

steps.title: Stateroom Guest Policies
steps.description: Packages generally apply to guests one and two on the reservation. Third and fourth stateroom guests are not automatically required to purchase the package, though separate eligibility and beverage regulations apply.

steps.title: Seamless Upgrades Anytime
steps.description: Guests who initially booked Princess Plus can upgrade to Princess Premier anytime before or during the cruise by paying the applicable $35 per person, per day difference.

steps.title: Check Historical Booking Terms
steps.description: Princess updates its package terms periodically. Guests sailing in 2026 who purchased packages prior to October 13, 2026 retain the specific terms and inclusions tied to their original booking date.

features.title: Core Fare Inclusions
features.description: Standard fares include full stateroom accommodation, multi-course main dining room meals, 24-hour buffet, poolside grills, Broadway-style theater entertainment, pool decks, fitness center, and Camp Discovery youth clubs.

features.title: Casual Dining Cover Fees
features.description: Guests on standard fares pay approximately $14.99 cover charges for multi-course casual dining prix fixe menus at venues like Alfredo's Pizzeria, which are complimentary under Plus (4 meals) and Premier (unlimited).

features.title: OceanNow & Room Service Fees
features.description: Standard fare guests pay a $14.99 per person per voyage OceanNow delivery access activation fee, and orders placed via stateroom phone carry a $5 delivery charge (both waived on Plus and Premier).

features.title: Crew Appreciation & Wi-Fi Added Separately
features.description: Without a package, crew appreciation is charged automatically to your onboard folio at $17–$19 per person, per day, and MedallionNet Wi-Fi costs approximately $24.99/day for 1 device.

advisor.name: Angela Hughes
advisor.title: CEO of Trips & Ships Luxury Travel
advisor.bio: With more than 40 years of luxury travel-industry experience and having visited over 121 countries across all seven continents, Angela Hughes provides expert guidance on evaluating Princess package economics, stateroom selection, and destination planning.
advisor.quote: Deciding between Princess Plus and Princess Premier isn't about counting features—it's about matching the package to your real vacation habits. If you plan to dine at Crown Grill and book shore excursions, Princess Premier pays for itself almost immediately.

faqs.question: What is the main difference between Princess Plus and Princess Premier?
faqs.answer: Princess Plus includes 15 eligible alcoholic drinks per day up to $15 each, Wi-Fi for one device, four casual dining meals per guest, crew appreciation, and delivery benefits. Princess Premier adds unlimited eligible drinks up to $20 each, unlimited qualifying specialty and casual dining, Wi-Fi for four devices, shore excursion credit, professional photos, and reserved theater seating.

faqs.question: How much more expensive is Princess Premier than Princess Plus?
faqs.answer: On most Princess ships, Premier costs $35 more per person, per day than Plus. The same difference applies to Sun Princess and Star Princess ($110 vs $75). For a seven-night cruise, the upgrade costs an additional $245 per guest ($490 for two guests).

faqs.question: Does Princess Plus include specialty dining?
faqs.answer: No. Princess Plus includes four qualifying casual dining meals per guest per voyage (such as Alfredo's Pizzeria, Kai Sushi, or Ocean Terrace). Specialty dining at venues like Crown Grill, Sabatini's, or The Catch by Rudi is not included as a general Plus package benefit.

faqs.question: Does Princess Premier include unlimited specialty dining?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under current published package terms, Princess Premier includes unlimited qualifying specialty and casual dining meals during the voyage. Venue participation, reservation requirements, and dining conditions apply.

faqs.question: Does Princess Plus include unlimited drinks?
faqs.answer: No. Princess Plus includes up to 15 eligible alcoholic drinks per guest per day, with a maximum eligible price of $15 per drink. Specialty coffees, teas, fountain sodas, and other eligible non-alcoholic beverages are also included under package terms.

faqs.question: Does Princess Premier include unlimited drinks?
faqs.answer: Princess Premier includes unlimited eligible beverages priced up to $20 each under current package terms, with no daily limit on alcoholic beverages. Beverage exclusions and responsible-service policies still apply.

faqs.question: Does Princess Premier include shore excursions?
faqs.answer: Princess Premier includes eligible shore excursion credit: $100 per guest for cruises of 6–9 days, $200 for 10–20 days, and $300 for voyages of 21 days or longer. Credit is subject to eligibility, availability, and the terms of the sailing.

faqs.question: How many devices can I use with each package?
faqs.answer: Princess Plus includes MedallionNet Max Wi-Fi for one device per guest. Princess Premier includes up to four devices per guest, allowing multiple smartphones, tablets, and laptops to remain connected simultaneously.

faqs.question: Does Princess Premier include crew gratuities?
faqs.answer: Yes. Crew appreciation is included in the current Princess Premier package under applicable terms. It is also included in Princess Plus.

faqs.question: Can I upgrade from Princess Plus to Princess Premier?
faqs.answer: Yes. Eligible guests can upgrade through Manage Booking, by contacting Princess, or through their travel advisor. The applicable price difference is based on the original package purchase and booking terms (typically $35 per person, per day).

faqs.question: Can I buy Princess Plus or Premier onboard?
faqs.answer: Yes. Princess allows eligible guests to purchase or upgrade packages onboard within the permitted purchase period. The published onboard rate is $5 more per person, per day than the lower pre-cruise rate ($75 for Plus, $110 for Premier on standard ships).

faqs.question: Do both guests in a stateroom need to purchase the same package?
faqs.answer: The package generally applies to guests one and two on the reservation. Third and fourth guests in the same stateroom are not automatically required to purchase the same package. Separate booking procedures and benefit-sharing rules apply.

faqs.question: Is Princess Plus or Princess Premier better for a seven-night cruise?
faqs.answer: Princess Plus may be a better fit for guests who want drinks, Wi-Fi, and a few casual dining experiences. Princess Premier may offer more value to guests who expect to use specialty dining, excursion credit, the higher beverage allowance, and professional photo benefits. Compare the $245 per-person seven-night price difference with the benefits you expect to use.
